stories.title: Newton SkyTrain promises meet an unresolved funding problem
stories.summary: Both major provincial parties have pledged support for SkyTrain service to Surrey’s Newton neighbourhood, CityNews reports October 21. The Conservatives propose working with Ottawa; the NDP points to $250 million in its platform for transit expansion in the area. That allocation should not be confused with a fully funded railway. TransLink CEO Kevin Quinn says a Newton extension would start from scratch, cost billions and arrive while long-term funding for existing services remains unresolved. For regional commuters, the new development is political support from both parties, rather than an approved construction schedule. Route planning, capital funding and operating money remain consequential questions before the promises translate into service.

stories.title: Thunderbird fixes password exposure during Exchange setup
stories.summary: Mozilla’s October 20 advisory rates Thunderbird 158.0.1 a high-impact security update. A bug in Exchange AutoDiscover sent entered credentials through an unencrypted HTTP request during account setup, potentially exposing the password to a network attacker. A separate XMPP flaw allowed crafted incoming requests to inject commands into automatic replies, potentially sending messages or changing contact settings without user interaction. That issue affects Thunderbird’s XMPP chat feature. Check the installed version and complete the appropriate update, particularly before configuring an Exchange account. These vulnerabilities have specific triggers; the advisory does not establish that every Thunderbird user has lost credentials. The email-client update is separate from yesterday’s Firefox patch.

stories.title: Build a useful demo pitch for Vancouver AI
stories.summary: BC + AI’s organizer invitation accepts working software, hardware and agent prototypes, including unfinished projects visitors can try. Recommend preparing a Murmur demonstration of Bluetooth access to an offline Pi, a Nekoni walkthrough of phone-accessible local document search, or an Embedible sensor-to-MCP demonstration. These fit the published prototype categories; acceptance still depends on organizer review. The concrete action is to describe what visitors can try, required space and power, and provide a short video through the linked pitch form. Source and application route: https://bc-ai.ca/communities/vancouver-ai/demos. No deadline is published, and the external form failed to load during this check, so confirm access before attempting submission. Include https://github.com/nekonihq/murmur or https://github.com/nekonihq/nekoni in the relevant walkthrough to support discovery and voluntary stars from interested developers. Direct hardware users to https://embedible.io/. No submission or demonstration slot is claimed.

events.title: V-Unframed opens immersive art to first-time visitors
events.description: The organizer confirms the 2026 dates, venue and ticket-selection page. Public exhibition tickets provide a 90-minute slot with more than 12 immersive experiences, each lasting five to 30 minutes. Staff assist newcomers with headsets, and most works are multilingual, English-only or language-free. Select a timed admission when planning the visit.

dining.title: Notch8 lists Winter Wonderland afternoon tea
dining.description: The restaurant’s official seasonal page confirms forthcoming service featuring cranberry-white-chocolate scones, smoked-salmon blini and holiday pastries. Adults are $79 before tax and gratuity. Service excludes December 19, 20, 24, 25 and 31, plus January 1. Dietary accommodations require 48 hours’ notice; reservation changes require 72 hours to avoid the stated $25-per-person cancellation fee. Use the page’s reservation link to check a particular sitting. The page verifies a dated seasonal offering but does not identify its announcement date.
